extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and developing writers looking for classes, workshops, fellowships, or one-on-one consulting (including teens and writers of color)
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and understanding GrubStreet's suite of creative-writing offerings (classes, workshops, intensives, fellowships, consulting, and special series) to match a writer's skill level and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Roadmap (goal-based course selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: We've created a simple, goal-based roadmap to help you find the perfect GrubStreet course for your writing needs. Whether you're just starting or getting ready to publish, we have classes for every stage of your writing journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roadmap organizes offerings by writer goals/stages (Discover, Create, Explore, Progress, Perspective, Polish, Publish) so learners can pick classes aligned to their current objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Enrollment / Broad Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: With nearly a thousand classes to choose from every year, GrubStreet programs cater to a wide range of writing genres and are open to anyone with an interest in creative writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No narrow prerequisites implied — choose based on interest and level; volume of classes supports diverse schedules and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program format options
rubrics_metrics.description: Program types offered include Multi-Week Workshops, Short Classes, Online Experience, Teen Program, Intensives, Contemporary Craft Series, Manuscript Month, Incubators, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select format based on time commitment, depth of feedback desired, and whether in-person or online is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary Craft Series design
rubrics_metrics.description: GrubStreet’s Contemporary Craft Series brings you low-cost opportunities to learn directly from some of the most influential voices in contemporary literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each live, online seminar focuses on a unique craft topic, includes Q&A, and offers fresh insights you can apply to your writing right away — good for targeted skill development and exposure to practitioner insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Month focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking place in May 2025, GrubStreet’s Manuscript Month is here to give you permission to dedicate a full month to take serious steps in your writing and publishing journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes workshops and online sessions; intended for concentrated, deadline-driven progress on a manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boston Writers of Color (BWOC) support offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: GrubStreet’s Boston Writers of Color (BWOC) offers literary support funding, free writing sessions, a network of BIPOC writers and artistic leaders, and a variety of free events that focus on community, artistic growth, and publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic supports include funding, community-building, resources and submission lists, and FAQs tailored to writers of color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom Consulting (one-on-one services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Like personal trainers for your writing life, our consultants work one-on-one with writers to help them finish drafts, set writing goals, or revise their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consulting to polish manuscripts before agent review, get focused feedback on a story, or seek career/advice; consultants cover all genres and adapt to individual objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships and scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: GrubStreet offers unique fellowships that support writers and writing instructors in developing their craft and finding writing community that can sustain them for years to come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Summer Teen Writing Fellowship, Emerging Writer Fellowship, Teaching Fellowship for Black Writers — these provide funding, mentorship, and community support; check each fellowship’s eligibility and application details on its page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teen-specific programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Teen Program offerings such as Teen Summer Writing Sessions and Teen Summer Writing Fellowship support adolescent writers with dedicated sessions and fellowship opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes application advice from past teen fellows and multi-year listings of fellows — useful for prospective teen applicants evaluating fit and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program page components to evaluate offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual program pages include Schedule & Curriculum, Meet the Instructor, The Students (or Student Achievements & Testimonials), How to Apply, Fellowships/Scholarships, and FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these components to assess time commitment, instructor fit, expected outcomes, application requirements, financial assistance, and participant experiences when choosing a program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-specific tools and generators
rubrics_metrics.description: GrubStreet provides Novel Generators (Young Adult, Romance, Mystery/Thriller, Fall Novel), Memoir Generator, and other tools to help start projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators function as prompts/structuring tools to jumpstart projects and can be used alongside classes or incubators.
